notes: NOT VALIDATED end-to-end -- unlike glaucoma (plans/plan_glaucoma.txt), no independent held-out dataset was found/used to confirm real-world accuracy (plans/plan_AMD.txt sections 3-4: every easily-accessible AMD dataset either overlaps with ODIR-5K or requires gated access). Training log shows classic overfitting signs (train_loss collapsed to ~0.0001 by epoch ~12, val_recall pinned at 1.0 for 18/25 epochs) on a small (~900 image, 6-source) dataset -- the 99.1% val_f1 above is almost certainly inflated (near-duplicate images across the 6 source datasets are not caught by exact-hash dedup, and the AMD-labeled samples skew toward advanced/textbook-obvious cases) and should NOT be read as real-world accuracy. Deployed anyway per explicit user decision (not a priority feature for this project) -- disclaimer in the UI/response must reflect this is substantially less validated than glaucoma or multidisease, not just 'experimental' in the generic sense. Training images were also pre-processed by the dataset author with gamma correction + CLAHE (exact original parameters unknown) -- inference/amd_engine.py applies its own gamma+CLAHE approximation (see gamma/clahe_* fields above) before classification to reduce train/inference distribution mismatch, but this is a best-effort match, not a verified replication of the original parameters.
